messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The issue described in the bug report is that when invoking SummaryStatistics.setVarianceImpl(new Variance(true/false)) (i.e., setting the variance implementation explicitly) and then adding values, calling getStandardDeviation() produces NaN.

Looking at the code:

1. getStandardDeviation() checks the number of observations (n) and if n>1 it returns the square root of getVariance().
2. getVariance() returns varianceImpl.getResult().
3. setVarianceImpl() sets the varianceImpl field, but only if no values have been added (checked by checkEmpty()); if values were added, it throws an exception.
4. addValue(double) increments multiple statistics including varianceImpl if it is not an instance of Variance. Specifically:
   - if (!(varianceImpl instanceof Variance)) { varianceImpl.increment(value); }
5. Variance.getResult() returns:
   - NaN if no values (n==0),
   - 0 if one value,
   - else moment.m2/(n-1) or moment.m2/n depending on bias correction.

The problem is that after using setVarianceImpl(new Variance(false)) on a fresh SummaryStatistics and then adding values, getStandardDeviation() returns NaN.

Key point: addValue() will not update the varianceImpl.increment(value) if varianceImpl is an instance of Variance because of the condition on line 161 (varianceImpl.increment(value) is only called if varianceImpl is NOT an instance of Variance). This means that the internal varianceImpl object (which is a Variance instance) is never updated when adding values.

Because varianceImpl.increment() is never called, varianceImpl's internal state variables like moment.n and moment.m2 remain at their initial state, so calling varianceImpl.getResult() returns NaN (as moment.n is zero).

Hence, getVariance() returns NaN and so does getStandardDeviation().

The failing test sets Mean explicitly to a new Mean() instance, but in variance case, if we override the default Variance with a new Variance instance, addValue() does not update it, so getStandardDeviation() returns NaN.

Summary:
The bug occurs because the addValue method skips incrementing the custom varianceImpl if it is an instance of Variance. This makes the variance state remain empty and causes getVariance() and getStandardDeviation() to return NaN.

This explains the bug where setting varianceImpl to a new Variance causes getStandardDeviation to produce NaN since the variance state is never updated during addValue.

Next, I will suggest which methods to fix.
org.apache.commons.math.stat.descriptive.SummaryStatistics.addValue(double)
org.apache.commons.math.stat.descriptive.SummaryStatistics.setVarianceImpl(org.apache.commons.math.stat.descriptive.StorelessUnivariateStatistic)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
